title.narrative: Ethiopia has introduced “choice awareness” in the decision-making process and taken ownership of the preparation of Ethiopia Energy Outlook.
Decision-making regarding the type and amount of energy development is guided by state-of-the-art analyses.

target.value: Learnings from NEP 2.0 has been completed and accepted. Consultations has been done and there are a general consensus about the report among key stakeholders.

actual.value:
A study was conducted to assess the achievements to date and identify both successes and barriers hindering further progress.
The initial draft of the study report was circulated among partners, and its findings were presented during meetings at partner institutions to gather feedback and build consensus. Following this, a draft final report was prepared and presented at a stakeholder workshop
The report has since been circulated among partner institutions and key stakeholders for further feedback and input.
Discussions are underway regarding the publication of the report.

target.value: Informed Energy planning adopted at MoWE and EEP based on transparent state-of-the-art analyses.

title.narrative: EEP supported to prepare and conduct international standard wind tenders.
EEP successfully completed the 2 auction of wind power plants.

target.value: Assessment of the wind tendering process conducted to identified gaps and agree on actions to fill the gaps

actual.value:
Assesment is pending, the EEP has not been interested / been ready to share document from the tendering process
Project office at the ministry of finance has reached out to the DEA, Christmas 2023.
The Outcome has in may facilitated a workshop in Addis between MOWE, EEP and the project office with topic of de risking and financing of wind projects

target.value: DEA team identified areas for the technical support started working with EEP
The auction for additional wind power plants completed with financial transaction completed with active participation of EEP and MoF IPP department
EEP and MoF IPP department took the lead and completed the auction for additional wind power plants with minimum support from partners. Increased focus on high-wind sites

title.narrative: Capacity in energy planning and modelling to conduct analyses and prepare Ethiopia energy outlook is created at EEP, EEU and MoWE and a joint Ethiopian planning platform possibly with the participation of selected universities
Number of EEP, EEU and MoWE staff members trained in energy modelling and documented being able to conduct analyses and prepared energy outlook.

target.value: Discussions started and trainees identified from each organisation

Workshop on using key types of models has been done. The models could be Balmorel, PSS/E or PowerFactory and Sisyfos. Participants from MoWE, EEP and universities. Additional 10 EEP, EEU and MOWE staff members trained in energy planning and modelling Challenges with using Balmorel in the cloud has been solved.

actual.value: The workshop on available energy planning tools and training of additional staff members took place during a mission in Nov 2023. The additional staff that were trained comprised MoWE and EEP employees only. EEU staff did not attend. The power sector working group still encounter occasional issues when accessing the cloud server.

target.value: Additional 10 EEP, EEU and MoWE trained staff members in energy plan-ning and modelling actively took part in the preparation of the second Ethiopian energy outlook mentored and coached by DEA
University level test in planning and modelling performed for EEP (including NLDC) and MoWE staff. At least 10 staff pass the test
EEP, EEU and MoWE staff members took the ownership of the preparation of the third Ethiopian energy outlook with minimum mentoring from DEA
Additional 10 staff pass the planning and modelling test. EEP, EEU and MoWE joint team launched the fourth Ethiopian energy outlook independently

title.narrative: Development of dynamic trade with neighbouring countries, with import and export of electricity
Mechanism for a market based energy trade in place. Degree of dynamic trade (only in dry years, monthly, hourly variation). Bilateral of multilateral arrangement (EAPP)

target.value: Initial discussions with EAPP started and in the review of the EEP masterplan the interaction with all neighbours including the import/export between countries will be studied.
SMechanism for dynamic trade is formulated and presented for relevant stakeholders. Agreement of first steps for practical dynamic trade.
Dynamic trade with three or more countries.
General mechanism for a dynamic trade in place EAPP open for trade (Day-ahead market) and Ethiopia is active

title.narrative: Ethiopia Energy Outlook prepared and published and used to guide energy policy and planning
EEP master plan preparation and revision including energy sector policy and planning is done based on the analyses in the Ethiopia energy outlook

target.value: Review of EEP master plan started
Update of the EEP 10 years Master Plan published

actual.value: The 10 years Master Plan document has not yet been published. Drafting of the detailed input and result reports is still ongoing. To aid publication, a Summary Report has been drafted by RDE. The Ethiopian Energy Outlook 2024 project was initiated, engaging the following partners: MoWE, EEP, EEU and PEA. Working groups have been established for the respective Energy Landscape and Power Sector Analysis sections of the Energy Outlook report. Preliminary power sector development scenarios have been developed and analysed. Results of these scenarios were presented to stakeholders during a workshop in May.

target.value: The second Ethiopian Energy Outlook is prepared and published in partnership with DEA
Publication of the third Ethiopian Energy Outlook and is done by MoWE and EEP team with minimum mentoring support from DEA.

title.narrative: Ethiopian universities are partnered with Danish universities to furnish them with the necessary capacity to continuously supply the energy sector with well-trained man-power.
2-3 Ethiopian universities prepared and implemented international level curriculums focusing on energy sources assessment, planning, development and management

target.value: Universities identified and initial discussion for curriculum development and other exercises started

Mapping of relevant curriculum and research within wind power, energy planning, energy modelling and social aspects of energy has been completed. Three universities in Ethiopia are selected to partner with Danish universities and capacity assessment conducted and targets identified and agreed to enable them to conduct international level courses

actual.value: The university curriculum mapping task has been completed. A report presenting the findings has been finalised. The three universities have been selected: Adama Science and Technology University, Addis Ababa Institute of Technology, and Mekelle University. Currently planning capacity building activities focussed on curriculum development in 1) energy planning and 2) modelling and wind energy development. The first workshop is expected to take place in December 2024.

target.value: TBD following the capacity assessment and partnership agreements between the Ethiopian and Danish Universities

title.narrative: EEP supported to put in place the necessary framework for procurement of wind power production

Conditions for a regulatory, institutional, and financial framework that streamlines pre-development of wind projects reducing risk for investors and lenders including an efficient wind tendering process is developed and institutionalised. Importance of general business environment is understood.

target.value: • A number of activities with relation to wind power has been done, including mapping the need for training in wind power model (Wind Pro and Wind Atlas Analysis and Application program, WASP).
17 wind masts from the previous wind project has been handed over to EEP. The status of masts will be described, including investigating if data can continued to be published.

actual.value:
Wind mast data has been accessed at one site, data quality is good.
The masts are functional but the equipment needs to be calibrated.
EEP wants to move 8 masts. The DEA has looked into if any partner could help fund this project.
The outcome has in collaboration with MOWE and the EEP completed a training sessions in WAsP using data from one Windmast, Gode site.

target.value: 400 MW additional wind power added. More than 200 MW from IPP

title.narrative: Enabling environment and transparent framework for lowering the cost of wind pow-er development created
Wind power production increased as a result of the use of cost and time efficient procurement systems, procedures and best practices

target.value: No target for the year

title.narrative: Economic dispatch of all generation. Hydropower is absorbing the variation in generation from wind and solar. Minimal curtailment of wind and solar.
Degree of curtailment of wind and solar power in %
